1 Generate a `DESIGN.md` file at the project root that captures the current visual design system, so AI agents generating new screens stay on-brand. 2 3 DESIGN.md follows the [official DESIGN.md format spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-labs-code/design.md/main/docs/spec.md): optional YAML frontmatter carrying machine-readable design tokens, followed by up to eight markdown sections in a fixed order. **Tokens are normative; prose provides context for how to apply them.** Sections may be omitted when not relevant, but those present stay in the specified order. Use the canonical headings below so the file remains portable across DESIGN.md-aware tools. 4 5 ## The frontmatter: token schema 6 7 The YAML frontmatter is the machine-readable layer. It's what Stitch's linter validates and what the live panel renders tiles from. Keep it tight; every entry should correspond to a token the project actually uses. 8 9 ```yaml 10 --- 11 name: 12 description: 13 colors: 14 primary: "#b8422e" 15 neutral-bg: "#faf7f2" 16 # ...one entry per extracted color; key = descriptive slug 17 typography: 18 display: 19 fontFamily: "Cormorant Garamond, Georgia, serif" 20 fontSize: "clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 4.5rem)" 21 fontWeight: 300 22 lineHeight: 1 23 letterSpacing: "normal" 24 body: 25 # ... 26 rounded: 27 sm: "4px" 28 md: "8px" 29 spacing: 30 sm: "8px" 31 md: "16px" 32 components: 33 button-primary: 34 backgroundColor: "{colors.primary}" 35 textColor: "{colors.neutral-bg}" 36 rounded: "{rounded.sm}" 37 padding: "16px 48px" 38 button-primary-hover: 39 backgroundColor: "{colors.primary-deep}" 40 --- 41 ``` 42 43 Rules that matter: 44 45 - **Token refs** use `{path.to.token}` (e.g. `{colors.primary}`, `{rounded.md}`). Components may reference primitives; primitives may not reference each other. 46 - **Colors accept any valid CSS color string.** Hex is the recommended default for portability, but preserve an incumbent `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `oklch()`, wide-gamut, or mixed-color value when it is the project's normative source. Never split the source of truth without explicit reason. 47 - **Component sub-tokens** are limited to 8 props: `backgroundColor`, `textColor`, `typography`, `rounded`, `padding`, `size`, `height`, `width`. Shadows, motion, focus rings, backdrop-filter: none of those fit. Carry them in the sidecar (Step 4b). 48 - **Scale keys are open-ended.** Use whatever names the project already uses (`oxblood-deep`, `surface-container-low`). Don't rename to Material defaults. 49 - **Variants are naming convention, not schema.** `button-primary` / `button-primary-hover` / `button-primary-active` as sibling keys. 50 51 ## The markdown body: eight sections (canonical order) 52 53 1. `## Overview` 54 2. `## Colors` 55 3. `## Typography` 56 4. `## Layout` 57 5. `## Elevation & Depth` 58 6. `## Shapes` 59 7. `## Components` 60 8. `## Do's and Don'ts` 61 62 Omit irrelevant sections rather than filling them with invented rules. Put responsive layout in Layout, depth in Elevation & Depth, radius and form language in Shapes, and per-component behavior in Components. Unknown sections are preserved by the format, but new visual guidance should use the canonical structure whenever it fits. 63 64 ## When to run 65 66 - New-work found a coherent incumbent visual system but no `DESIGN.md`. 67 - The first implementation of a new world is complete and its provisional decisions need to be carbonized. 68 - An existing `DESIGN.md` is stale (the design has drifted). 69 - Before a large redesign, to capture the current state as a reference. 70 71 If a `DESIGN.md` already exists, **do not silently overwrite it**. Show the user the existing file first. Ask with Codex's structured user-input/question tool when available, or directly in chat if it is not, and wait for the answer before continuing. The choice is refresh, overwrite, or merge. 72 73 ## Two paths 74 75 - **Scan mode** (default): the project has design tokens, components, or rendered output. Extract, then confirm descriptive language. Use when there's code to analyze. 76 - **Seed mode**: the project is pre-implementation. Ensure PRODUCT.md exists, then reuse new-work's visual-world workshop and write its directional DESIGN.md seed. Re-run in scan mode once there's code. 77 78 Decide by scanning first (Scan mode Step 1). If the scan finds no tokens, no component files, and no rendered site, offer seed mode; don't silently switch. `$impeccable document --seed` requests new-work's world workshop, but it does not authorize replacing coherent code: when an incumbent system exists, offer scan mode or route an explicit identity-replacement request through new-work. 79 80 ## Scan mode (approach C: auto-extract, then confirm descriptive language) 81 82 ### Step 1: Find the design assets 83 84 Search the codebase in priority order: 85 86 1. **CSS custom properties**: grep for `--color-`, `--font-`, `--spacing-`, `--radius-`, `--shadow-`, `--ease-`, `--duration-` declarations in CSS files (usually `src/styles/`, `public/css/`, `app/globals.css`, etc.). Record name, value, and the file it's defined in. 87 2. **Tailwind config**: if `tailwind.config.{js,ts,mjs}` exists, read the `theme.extend` block for colors, fontFamily, spacing, borderRadius, boxShadow. 88 3. **CSS-in-JS theme files**: styled-components, emotion, vanilla-extract, stitches; look for `theme.ts`, `tokens.ts`, or equivalent. 89 4. **Design token files**: `tokens.json`, `design-tokens.json`, Style Dictionary output, W3C token community group format. 90 5. **Component library**: scan the main button, card, input, navigation, dialog components. Note their variant APIs and default styles. 91 6. **Global stylesheet**: the root CSS file usually has the base typography and color assignments. 92 7. **Visible rendered output**: if browser automation tools are available, load the live site and sample computed styles from key elements (body, h1, a, button, .card). This catches values that tokens miss. 93 94 ### Step 2: Auto-extract what can be auto-extracted 95 96 Build a structured draft from the discovered tokens. For each token class: 97 98 - **Colors**: Group into Primary / Secondary / Tertiary / Neutral (the Material-derived roles Stitch uses). If the project only has one accent, express it as Primary + Neutral; omit Secondary and Tertiary rather than inventing them. 99 - **Typography**: Map observed sizes and weights to the Material hierarchy (display / headline / title / body / label). Note font-family stacks and the scale ratio. 100 - **Elevation**: Catalogue the shadow vocabulary. If the project is flat and uses tonal layering instead, that's a valid answer; state it explicitly. 101 - **Components**: For each common component (button, card, input, chip, list item, tooltip, nav), extract shape (radius), color assignment, hover/focus treatment, internal padding. 102 - **Layout + spacing**: Extract grid, container, breakpoint, rhythm, and density behavior into Layout. 103 - **Shapes**: Extract radius, corner, border, clipping, and recurring form behavior into Shapes. 104 105 ### Step 2b: Stage the frontmatter 106 107 From the auto-extracted tokens, draft the YAML frontmatter now (you'll write it at the top of DESIGN.md in Step 4). This is the machine-readable layer: what the live panel and Stitch's linter consume. 108 109 - **Colors**: one entry per extracted color. Key = descriptive slug (`oxblood-deep`, `editorial-magenta`, not `blue-800`). Value = whichever format the project treats as canonical (OKLCH or hex; see the frontmatter rules above). Don't split the source of truth: one format in the frontmatter, don't redefine the same token in prose with a different value. 110 - **Typography**: one entry per role (`display`, `headline`, `title`, `body`, `label`). Typography is an object; include only the props that are real for the project (`fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `fontFeature`, `fontVariation`). 111 - **Rounded / Spacing**: whatever scale steps the project actually uses, keyed by whatever scale name the project uses (`sm` / `md` / `lg`, or `surface-sm`, or numeric steps). 112 - **Components**: one entry per variant (`button-primary`, `button-primary-hover`, `button-ghost`). Reference primitives via `{colors.X}`, `{rounded.Y}`. If a variant needs a property Stitch's 8-prop set doesn't cover (shadow, focus ring, backdrop-filter), carry the full snippet in the sidecar instead. 113 114 Skip anything the project doesn't have. Empty scale keys or fabricated tokens pollute the spec. 115 116 ### Step 3: Ask the user for qualitative language 117 118 The following require creative input that cannot be auto-extracted. Otherwise synthesize in OKLCH. 329 330 #### Narrative mapping 331 332 Pull directly from the DESIGN.md you just wrote: 333 334 - `narrative.northStar` → the `**Creative North Star: "..."**` line from Overview 335 - `narrative.overview` → the philosophy paragraphs from Overview 336 - `narrative.keyCharacteristics` → the bulleted `**Key Characteristics:**` list 337 - `narrative.rules` → every `**The [Name] Rule.** [body]` across all sections, tagged with `section` 338 - `narrative.dos` / `narrative.donts` → the bullet lists from Do's and Don'ts verbatim 339 340 Do not reword. Mention that `.impeccable/design.json` was also written alongside; the live panel will now render this project's actual button/input/nav primitives instead of generic approximations. 346 3. That pass will extract real tokens and generate the sidecar." 389 390 Your own write is the freshest source; no reload needed. 391 392 ## Style guidelines 393 394 - **Frontmatter first, prose second.** Tokens go in the YAML frontmatter; prose contextualizes them. Put motion guidance with the world or component it affects rather than creating a token group the schema does not support. 397 - **Descriptive > technical**: "Gently curved edges (8px radius)" > "rounded-lg". These are memorable, citable, and much stickier for AI consumers than bullet lists. Stitch's own outputs use them heavily ("The No-Line Rule", "The Ghost Border Fallback"). Aim for 1-3 per section. 401 - **Be decisive where evidence is decisive.** Use hard language for actual invariants and softer language for provisional guidance. 402 - **Use concrete audit tests only when they are grounded in the observed system or a confirmed user decision.** A one-sentence test beats a paragraph of principle. 403 - **Reference PRODUCT.md selectively.** Product truth explains why the world fits; it does not supply page composition or a visual don't-list by default. 404 - **Group colors by role**, not by hex-order or hue-order. Stop at what's actually reused; one-offs pollute the system. 410 - Don't invent components that don't exist. If the project only has buttons and cards, only document those. 411 - Don't overwrite an existing DESIGN.md without asking. 412 - Don't duplicate content from PRODUCT.md. DESIGN.md is strictly visual. 413 - Don't replace canonical sections with near-synonyms. Put layout and responsive behavior in `Layout`; put motion with the affected world or component. 414 - Don't rename sections even slightly. "Colors" not "Color Palette & Roles". "Typography" not "Typography Rules". Tooling parsing depends on exact headers. 415 - Don't duplicate token values between frontmatter and prose. If a color is in `colors.primary` as hex, the prose can name it and describe its role but should not reassert a different hex. The frontmatter is normative. 416 - Don't invent frontmatter token groups outside Stitch's schema (no `motion:`, `breakpoints:`, `shadows:` at the top level). Stitch's Zod schema only accepts `colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`. Anything else belongs in the sidecar's `extensions`. 417

# Design System: mrmr Signal Box

This system covers `/manage/` and `/dashboard/`. The setup atlas in `wiki/` is a
separate document with its own look, recorded in the root `DESIGN.md`.

## Overview

**Creative North Star: "The Signal Box"**

In mrmr a model may ask, but fixed machinery decides what moves. These pages show
that machinery. Each monitor is a track through Collect, Judge, Decide and Effect,
so a fault names the stage it stopped at, and the page headline says it in words.

Someone opens these pages to check that all is well, usually for a few seconds. One
sentence answers that, the tracks show where any problem is, and a link leads to the
stored evidence. Density is that of a working tool: tables, not cards.

**Key Characteristics:**

- The graphite top bar and cream ground are the only large colour areas.
- Colour reports state. Almost nothing is coloured for decoration.
- Lamps and tracks are the signature, reused at every scale.
- The page says only what the runtime has recorded.

## Colors

A warm neutral panel, with a small fixed set of signal colours that each mean one thing.

### Primary

- **Graphite:** top bar, primary buttons, track rails, lamp rims and text.

### Secondary

- **Clear Green:** the latest record for this stage succeeded.
- **Signal Amber:** look at this, or deliberately held back in shadow. Also the
  active navigation underline and text selection.
- **Stop Red:** the latest record failed, or effects are blocked. Use the ink value
  for text and the base value for lamps.
- **Lunar White (the raised colour):** configured, which is not evidence of anything.
- **Dark Lamp Grey:** paused, ignored, or nothing recorded.

### Tertiary

- **Draft Violet:** draft, not running. The unsaved-changes bar and the guide's
  current step.

### Neutral

- **Signal Cream (ground):** the page field.
- **Pale Cream (surface):** panels, tracks and tables.
- **Raised Cream:** inputs and secondary buttons.
- **Rule lines:** panel borders, with the soft value between table rows.
- **Muted Grey-Green:** secondary text, at 4.5:1 or better on every cream.

### Named Rules

**The One Meaning Rule.** A signal colour means its one state on every screen. If a
colour is not reporting state, it should not be there.

**The Configuration Is Not Evidence Rule.** A stage that is only configured gets a
lunar lamp, never green. Green needs a stored record behind it.

**The Lamp Speaks Rule.** Every lamp sits beside text that states the same thing, so
no state depends on colour perception.

## Typography

**Display Font:** none separate; the system sans carries headings.
**Body Font:** system sans.
**Label/Mono Font:** the system monospace, for code and data only.

**Character:** The platform's own sans, set tightly and heavily in headings. It keeps
the single binary free of font assets and makes the pages feel native to the machine.

### Hierarchy

- **Headline:** the page `h1`. On the status pages it is the answer itself, and it
  turns red when something has stopped.
- **Title:** section headings and event names.
- **Body:** running text, up to 72ch. Numerals are tabular everywhere.
- **Label:** help text, table headers and stage details.
- **Code:** YAML, raw JSON and trace data.

### Named Rules

**The Sentence First Rule.** Status is a written sentence before it is a number. Do
not replace it with a row of metric tiles.

## Layout

A full-width page with a 40px gutter on desktop and 16px on phones. The top bar sits
above a page heading, with freshness and refresh at the right of that heading. Pages
with supporting material use a main column and a narrow side column. On phones
those columns stack, navigation drops to its own row, and tables reflow into stacked
records. Nothing may scroll the page sideways at 390px.

## Elevation & Depth

Flat, using tonal layers from ground to surface to raised, with 1px rules. The one
shadow in the system belongs to the floating notice bar, which sits over content.

## Shapes

Gently rounded panels and tracks (8px) and controls (6px). Lamps are full circles
with a thick graphite rim, and rails are solid straight lines, like a drawn panel
diagram.

## Components

### Lamp

A circle with a graphite rim, filled by state. It always comes with text.

### Track

A monitor name beside a rail with four stage lamps, each labelled with its stage and
a detail such as "Failed 26s ago". The same rail is reused inside event detail, for
the path one event took, and as the guide's progress line.

### Buttons

- **Default:** raised cream with a rule border.
- **Primary:** graphite with cream text, for the main action in a view.
- **Danger:** stop-red text and border on raised cream.
- **Quiet:** an underlined text button for minor actions.

### Notices

A floating bar at the bottom centre of the viewport. Info notices clear on
navigation. Errors stay until dismissed, on stop red.

### Draft bar

A violet-washed bar that sticks to the top of Configure only while a draft exists,
holding Save and Review and apply. When nothing is pending it stays quiet.

### Tables

Pale cream with a rule border, small muted headers, soft row rules and tabular
numerals. The Outcome column shows a lamp and its words.

### Navigation

Text links on graphite. The current page is white with an amber underline.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do:

- **Do** write the status headline from runtime data, and name the track and stage.
- **Do** reuse the track rail wherever a sequence of pipeline stages appears.
- **Do** put model and event text on the page with `textContent` only.
- **Do** keep raw JSON available in a disclosure, below the readable version.

### Don't:

- **Don't** use violet for anything except a draft that is not running.
- **Don't** show green for configuration, or for anything without a stored record.
- **Don't** use inline style attributes or inline scripts. The pages' content security
  policy blocks them.
- **Don't** use monospace for anything other than code and data.

content.text:
I've rebuilt both `/manage/` and `/dashboard/` with a new look called Signal Box, and all checks pass. Nothing is committed, and your live deployment still runs the old UI. I checked it against a local preview with synthetic data, not real traffic.

## What changed
- **Status at a glance:** the page headline now answers "is all well?" in words, such as "Printer is stopped at Collect".
- **Monitors as tracks:** each monitor runs through Collect, Judge, Decide and Effect, with a lamp and text at each stage, so a fault shows where it stopped.
- **Colour:** green, amber, red, white and grey each report one state, and violet only ever means an unsaved draft. A stage that's only configured gets a white lamp, never green.
- **Overview:** it now leads with a "Needs your attention" table, and the permanent amber banner is gone.
- **Activity:** events are in a table instead of about 130px blocks, and event detail is readable, with raw JSON tucked behind a disclosure.
- **Configure:** the save bar only stands out when you have a draft.
- **Runtime:** the audit log loads on arrival instead of staying blank until clicked.
- **Phones:** tables become stacked records and nothing scrolls sideways at 390px, including with event detail open.
- **Unchanged:** the operator token stays in memory only, and Lock still clears private content.

I also fixed two small bugs: unbroken JSON in event traces was widening the phone layout, and a source that hadn't polled read "last poll started Not observed".

## Validation
- **Passing:** `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, the dashboard navigation test, and the real-Chrome management test at phone and desktop widths. After the last one-line fix I reran `gofmt`, the build, the two affected Go packages and those two browser tests, not the whole suite.
- **New tests:** route checks for the two new shared files, `signal.css` and `signal.js`.
- **Looked at:** rendered screens at 1440 and 390, including error, draft and empty states. Screenshots are in `.impeccable/review/`.
- **Finish review disposition: `fix`, then `ship`:** the one fix was the poll wording, now resolved. I ran this review inline rather than with a separate reviewer, so it isn't truly independent.

## Detector warnings left in place
- **`cream-palette`:** this flags the background, but cream is the look you picked.
- **`cramped-padding`:** this flags the table wrapper on the dashboard, but the table cells carry their own padding, so it's a false positive.

## Deviations from the sketch and previous UI
- **Decide lamp:** it's white rather than the sketch's green, because configuration isn't evidence.
- **Safety gate:** "off" also shows a white lamp.
- **"Operator access active" notice:** replaced with footer text.
- **New routes:** `/dashboard/signal.*` and `/manage/signal.*`. The `/manage/` ones are public, because the login page needs them before any token exists; they contain no runtime data.
- **System font:** I kept the system sans from the sketch rather than bundling a font, even though the design checklist normally discourages it. The app stays a single binary this way.

## Still open
- **Design doc:** I wrote it to `internal/dashboard/DESIGN.md`, which is untracked, so it's your call whether to commit it. I left the root `DESIGN.md` alone because it covers the wiki atlas, and the tooling reads the new file for these pages.
- **Skipped sidecar:** I didn't write the optional `design.json` because the existing one belongs to the atlas, so Impeccable's live panel won't show these components.
- **`PRODUCT.md`:** it still describes only the wiki, and I didn't change it.

name = 'live-notify-20261031T221624Z'

env.clear()

before = state()

assert digest(root / 'mrmr') == expected_previous, 'Installed code changed'
assert digest(release / 'mrmr') == expected_binary, 'Release transfer mismatch'

unchanged = {str(p): digest(p) for p in (root / 'mrmr.yaml', unit, credentials, discord_file)}

backup.mkdir(mode=0o700)
installed = False
stopped = False

        shutil.copy2(source, backup / target)
    for filename in ('deployment.json', 'verification.json', 'source.tar.gz', 'INSTALL.md'):
        if (root / filename).exists():
            shutil.copy2(root / filename, backup / filename)
    (backup / 'serve.json').write_bytes(serve)
    source_db = sqlite3.connect('file:' + str(root / 'mrmr.db') + '?mode=ro', uri=True)

        assert saved_db.execute('SELECT MAX(version) FROM schema_migrations').fetchone()[0] == 9
        cursors = source_db.execute('SELECT name,cursor FROM source_cursors ORDER BY name').fetchall()

        counts = {table: source_db.execute('SELECT count(*) FROM ' + table).fetchone()[0] for table in ('events', 'decisions', 'executions', 'control_draft', 'control_evaluations')}
    finally:

    temporary = root / ('mrmr.' + name)

    temporary.chmod(0o700)
    with temporary.open('rb') as f:
        os.fsync(f.fileno())
    os.replace(temporary, root / 'mrmr')
    installed = True
    directory_fd = os.open(root, os.O_DIRECTORY)
    try:
        os.fsync(directory_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(directory_fd)
    systemctl('start')
    after = None
    for _ in range(30):

            break
        except (OSError, AssertionError, ValueError):
            time.sleep(0.5)
    assert after is not None, 'New runtime did not become ready'
    assert all(after[k] == before[k] for k in ('revision', 'document', 'draft', 'shadow_override')), 'Runtime configuration or draft changed'

    try:
        assert con.execute('PRAGMA integrity_check').fetchone()[0] == 'ok'
        assert con.execute('SELECT MAX(version) FROM schema_migrations').fetchone()[0] == 9
        for table, count in counts.items():
            assert con.execute('SELECT count(*) FROM ' + table).fetchone()[0] >= count, 'Stored records were lost'
        assert set(row[0] for row in con.execute('SELECT name FROM source_cursors')) == set(row[0] for row in cursors)
    finally:
        con.close()
    record = {'at': datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(), 'release': str(release), 'backup': str(backup), 'binary_sha256': expected_binary, 'previous_binary_sha256': expected_previous, 'commit': manif
    for p in (root / 'deployment.json', release / 'deployment.json'):
        p.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(json.dumps(record, indent=2))
except BaseException:
    if stopped:
        if installed:

            os.replace(root / 'mrmr.rollback', root / 'mrmr')

    raise SystemExit('Deployment failed; prior executable restart attempted. Inspect service state before retrying.')

## Problems on the live page
Both come from my redesign. I haven't fixed them, because that means another release and restart you haven't approved.
- **Overclaiming status:** the page says "All tracks clear" and shows a green Effect lamp for live rules, yet there are zero events and no decisions. Only collection is proven; the model path and notification delivery aren't. This breaks the design's own rule that configuration isn't evidence, and it affects the page's main job.
- **Empty events table:** on desktop, the "No events stored yet" message sits at the right edge instead of being centred.

## Deployment
- **Install:** mrmr restarted cleanly at 23:11 UTC with no automatic restarts, and the database schema is still version 9.
- **Unchanged:** the config file, service unit, credential files and Tailscale routes.
- **Backup:** `~/mrmr/backups/pre-signal-box-20261031T231111Z/`
- **Release notes and rollback steps:** `~/mrmr/releases/signal-box-20261031T231111Z/DEPLOYMENT.md`

## Verification
- **Before deploying:** race tests, `go vet` and the Chrome browser test passed on a clean copy of the commit.
- **Live assets:** all seven `/manage/` files match the commit over HTTPS.
- **Access guards:** a request without a token gets 401, and a foreign-origin request gets 403.
- **Monitors:** Plex and Hermes Dashboard both polled successfully after the restart, and the other named services are still active.
- **Browser:** the login page and read-only dashboard rendered at 390px and 1440px with no console errors or sideways scrolling.

## Not checked
- **Unlocked `/manage/` views on Marvin:** these need the operator token, and I didn't read it. A credential scan that would have read it was blocked, so I also left it out of the deploy script. You'll need to unlock the page and look; the same views passed the browser test locally.

|---|---|

- **Why `/dashboard/` fails in a browser:** `https://marvin.tail91529e.ts.net:8445/dashboard/` does reach mrmr, but it returns 401 without the operator token, including for the page's own files. A browser can't send that token when opening a URL directly, so the page won't load.

content.text:
The token removal is built and tested, but it isn't live: **the page on Marvin still asks for the token.** Claude Code's permission check blocked the production deploy, so I stopped there. The whole command was refused, so the commit (`af65860`) is only on your machine, and Marvin is unchanged and still running.

## What changes once deployed
- **No token for you:** opening `https://marvin.tail91529e.ts.net:8445/manage/` from your tailnet goes straight in, because Tailscale Serve tells mrmr you're `heath0xFF@github`. That's the only login on your tailnet, and it's the only one I'd allow.
- **Lock button:** it's hidden on this route, since a reload would let you straight back in.
- **Read-only dashboard:** `:8445/dashboard/` should also start working in a browser, with no SSH tunnel.

## What stays
- **The token isn't fully gone:** mrmr still needs it set to start, and it's still what `localhost` and SSH tunnels use. You'd just stop seeing it over Tailscale. Removing it completely would leave those routes with no login, so I kept it.
- **Protection against other websites:** the existing checks on request origin and write requests stay, and tests cover them with Tailscale login in use.

## The tradeoff
- **Local processes:** anything running on Marvin can reach the local port and fake the Tailscale login header, then change config or trigger notifications. Anything running as `heath`, such as Hermes, can already read the token file, so that's not new; other local accounts would gain this access.
- **Your devices:** any device signed in to your tailnet gets full management access with no second step. Tagged devices don't get in.

## Testing
- **Tests:** race tests and the Chrome browser test pass on a clean copy of the commit.
- **Local browser check:** your login goes straight in, while an unlisted login or `localhost` gets the token form.
- **Not tested on Marvin:** the real Tailscale header can't be confirmed until this is deployed. If the login doesn't match exactly, you'd just see the token form as you do now.

## What happens when you say go
1. Push `af65860` to the `signal-box-dashboard` branch.
2. Replace the binary on Marvin and add `-control-tailscale-user heath0xFF@github` to the service unit. That means a brief mrmr restart, with a backup first and automatic rollback if startup checks fail.
3. Check it live, including all five `/manage/` pages at phone and desktop widths, which I couldn't check last time.

**Reply "deploy it" and I'll retry.** If the permission check blocks it again, you'd need to add a Claude Code permission rule for it, or run the deploy yourself with `!`.
